text:
Eileen (SE): starting thread for MeridianRetail POC. They want streaming chat w/ tool calls -> internal order API, strict JSON schema validation on outputs, and a Go example for our SDK. Quick asks: ephemeral creds pattern, latency for 150-token responses at 200 rps, and pricing options (hosted vs reserved).
Sam (AE): theyre budget-conscious and asked whether streaming costs more than non-streaming. Also asked if we can do IP-restricted webhooks + mTLS.
Aisha (Eng): streaming itself is per-token like generation; no separate "+stream" surcharge. That said, low-latency targets (p95 <250ms) at 200rps point to reserved capacity to avoid noisy neighbors.
Eileen (SE): they explicitly want deterministic JSON output for downstream ingestion. Can we enforce schema and reject responses if invalid?
Aisha (Eng): yes: use structured_output_mode + strict_schema=true. We run the response through an output parser on the server side and can emit a schema_violation event. Optionally block the response and return 422 + error payload.
Ravi (Security): webhook hardening: require client to present mTLS cert + IP allowlist; we recommend a short webhook token rotated every 12h and posting events to a pre-provisioned queue (SQS/Kafka) rather than direct POSTs.
Noah (DevEx): Go SDK snippet (streaming chat + tool call) - small example they can drop into their service:
```go
ctx := context.Background()
// TokenProvider should return a fresh token before TTL expires
client := redwood.NewClient(redwood.WithTokenProvider(tokenProvider))
stream, err := client.ChatStream(ctx, "redwood-retail-1", redwood.ChatOptions{Streaming: true, Tools: []redwood.Tool{orderTool}})
if err != nil { log.Fatal(err) }
for ev := range stream.Events() {
    switch ev.Type {
    case redwood.EventTypeDelta:
        fmt.Print(ev.Delta.Text)
    case redwood.EventTypeToolCall:
        // SDK will surface tool request as JSON payload
        handleToolCall(ev.ToolRequest)
    case redwood.EventTypeDone:
        log.Println("stream done")
    }
}
```
Eileen (SE): nice. How does the ephemeral token rotation flow look for server-to-server (they dont want long-lived credentials on the order service)?
Noah (DevEx): pattern: 1) Redwood issues short-lived API tokens via our STS endpoint (15m default). 2) Customer runs a small credential-broker (lambda/container) that exchanges their long-live service credential for an STS token and returns to service. SDK TokenProvider polls TTL and refreshes when <60s. We can share a sample lambda.
IntegrationBot: sample STS broker and terraform snippets: https://internal.redwood/poctemplates/meridian-retail/ (demo manifest + ibm/azure/aws examples).
Sam (AE): pricing: can we send a hosted per-token estimate + a reserved 1-node monthly commitment for a 200 rps steady pilot? Need ballpark numbers to present by EOD.
Aisha (Eng): ballpark calc (very rough): 200 rps * 150 tokens * 3600s * 24h * 30d -> ~77.76B tokens/month (obviously pilot will be much lower; adjust to expected hours). For production-sensical monthly active hours assume 8h/day -> ~10.3B tokens. Hosted per-token price = $X per 1M tokens; reserved node = fixed monthly + lower per-token. I'll generate two scenarios: 8h/day pilot and 24/7 pilot.
Ravi (Security): questionnaire items: SOC2 status: we are SOC2 Type II audited (add standard boilerplate). KMS: Private deploy supports customer-managed KMS/HSM. Hosted uses Redwood KMS; enterprise EKM addendum available for Dedicated/Private. For tool callbacks require mTLS + IP allowlist + minimum TLS1.2.
Eileen (SE): schema example they asked for (simple order intent). They want server to reject if fields missing.
Aisha (Eng): sample schema (JSON Schema compact):
```json
{"type":"object","required":["order_id","intent","items"],"properties":{"order_id":{"type":"string"},"intent":{"type":"string","enum":["create","update","cancel"]},"items":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"object","required":["sku","qty"],"properties":{"sku":{"type":"string"},"qty":{"type":"integer","minimum":1}}}}}
```
Eileen (SE): perfect. Can we also surface schema_violation webhooks to customer telemetry?
Aisha (Eng): yes - you can configure a delivery endpoint; events include: violation_type, original_text, parsed_json, model_version. We also support auto-fallback to a safer model or returning a validation error per policy.
Sam (AE): blockers: 1) client legal wants EKM language in contract, 2) they want a POC runbook + demo app for onboarding, 3) need pricing by EOD.
Aisha (Eng): I'll push a short runbook (onboarding checklist + Dedicated node tuning) and 2 sample reserved quotes in ~3 hours.
Ravi (Security): I'll draft SOC2/KMS text and webhook mTLS/IP whitelist instructions and post the questionnaire answers.
Eileen (SE): next: Sam to confirm expected pilot hours/day and any compliance nuance; I'll schedule 30m tech kickoff for Tue 10am PT.
Sam (AE): confirmed I'll ask them for 8h/day pilot target and return by 5pm PT.
Eileen (SE): thanks folks :thumbsup: tagging @Aisha @Ravi @Noah for deliverables.
